budget_items.what_was_said: A member said the district had repeated elevator breakdowns last year because there was not enough money to fix or maintain it properly. It was cited as an example of a money problem that also became an operational problem because it was not planned for.

A member said the federal government's abrupt stopping and restarting of funding streams had created a serious problem for educational institutions nationally. They said it could have a direct impact on the district if fully implemented.
A member described wanting the district to be transparent about how much money it receives from the federal government and what is at risk, referencing a statement sent out after a funding scare.

budget_items.topic: Superintendent's budget-management skill as a desired trait
budget_items.what_was_said: A member praised a past superintendent's ability to track the different levels of the budget in her head and said this kind of budget fluency is a valued characteristic for the next superintendent.

decisions.decision: Committee agreed to finalize a short, bulleted version of the superintendent characteristics document to send to the full committee and the screening committee, saving the longer draft separately for reference.
Committee agreed each member would organize at least one staff or public listening session, coordinating dates through the chair to avoid scheduling overlaps.
Committee proceeded with the internal superintendent job posting using language largely copied from a prior posting, without a separate outside legal review.
Committee agreed that if the search moves to an external candidate process, they will bring in MASC (the state school committee association) to guide it.
Committee decided to post notice of a special Saturday meeting for the screening subcommittee by Thursday morning to satisfy the 48-hour posting requirement.
Committee decided the internal superintendent posting will not accept applications after the January 31 deadline, while screening-committee applications will still be accepted through that date.

public_comment.topic: A speaker from the floor thanked the chair and a fellow member for leading the superintendent search, saying they trusted them more than almost anyone with decisions affecting their children's future.

minutes.summary: This was a School Committee workshop devoted almost entirely to the superintendent search: shaping a short list of desired superintendent characteristics, planning staff and public listening sessions, and reviewing the internal hiring process, screening-committee makeup, and legal/HR considerations including possibly engaging MASC if the search goes external. The committee voted to table the screening-committee membership appointment to a Saturday meeting because an earlier notice had listed an incorrect application deadline, and closed with public comment thanking the chair and a colleague for the effort.

Members spent the workshop drafting a short list of desired superintendent characteristics to send to the full committee and the screening committee.
Each member agreed to organize at least one staff or public listening session on the search, coordinated through the chair.

why_it_matters: The superintendent search sets who leads the district's budget and staffing decisions for years; residents will see its results in who is appointed.
The screening-committee vote delay and the deadline mix-up mean residents watching that appointment should confirm the corrected Saturday meeting date and notice before assuming who is on it.
A member's comments about elevator repairs and federal funding volatility were offered as examples in the discussion, not as new budget figures or decisions.
